newsitem.title: JAPAN: Help on the way for those without toilet paper.
newsitem.headline: Help on the way for those without toilet paper.

text.p: Ever had one of those moments when you're out camping, in a public toilet or even at home and horror of horrors there's no toilet paper?
Relax, help is on the way in the form of a portable bottom washer that you can slip into a purse or a hip pocket.
Japan's largest battery maker Matsushita Battery Industrial Co Ltd announced on Tuesday that from February 1 it would start sales of a portable bidet-like gadget for those embarrassing moments.
The washer is about the size of an average paperback book and weighs just 275 grams (about 10 ounces), batteries included.
It holds 200 millilitres (7 fluid ounces) of water at a time which is squirted out through a collapsible nozzle. The units, which have adjustable water pressure, cost 11,000 yen ($91) each.
"Apart from uses stemming from hygenic reasons, the washer is useful on camping trips and when changing baby's nappies," a company spokeswoman said.
"More and more Japanese are installing toilets with automatic washing functions in their homes and many want to use them in public lavatories as well," the spokeswoman said.

The firm, which is a subsidiary of household appliance giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd, said in a statement that in 1990 only 10 percent of Japanese homes had toilets with washers, but the number was now 25 percent.
"Only five percent of hotels in Japan are equipped with such automatic wash toilets and the demand for portable ones is very large," the spokeswoman added.
It is not the first portable bidet, but Japanese pioneer Toto Ltd's version is bigger, needs assembling, involves detachable nozzles and is about 50 per cent more expensive. ($1=120 yen)
